movement_source: row 'Cash earnings', column Year to Sep 24 ($m) -> column Year to Sep 25 ($m)
headline: NAB's FY25 cash earnings were essentially flat: $7,091m against $7,102m, a fall of $11 million or 0.2% (ev-1, ev-13, ev-70). The bank leads with total net operating income of $20,813m, up 2.9% from $20,236m — revenue growth "with key drivers including volume growth and higher Markets & Treasury (M&T) income", and only 1.4% ex-M&T (ev-4, ev-45). Operating performance (underlying profit, income less operating expenses before impairment) rose 1.3% to $10,965m from $10,823m (ev-6, ev-47, ev-77). Statutory net profit fell further, down $201m or 2.9% to $6,759m from $6,960m (ev-10, ev-13, ev-71), because non-cash items widened: acquisitions, disposals and business closures cost $295m after tax versus $4m (a $291m deterioration), partly offset by a $34m swing in hedging and fair value volatility to +$28m (ev-11, ev-72, ev-73). Revenue growth of +$577m was absorbed almost exactly by higher expenses (+$435m, headline), a higher impairment charge (+$105m) and higher tax and minorities (+$48m).

drivers.columns: Year to Sep 25 vs Year to Sep 24
drivers.narrative: NII "increased by $644 million or 3.8%", including a $74m decrease from economic hedges offset in other operating income; excluding it the underlying rise was $718m or 4.3%, "due to higher average interest earning assets and net interest margin" (ev-14, ev-2). AIEA rose 2.3% to $1,001.2bn, GLAs +5.9%, deposits +7.4% (ev-26, ev-52).

drivers.bank_label: Increase due to change in average balance
drivers.narrative: The volume and rate analysis allocates +$1,204m of the $646m NII change to average balance (ev-34). AIEA grew 2.3% "reflecting growth primarily in business lending and, to a lesser extent, in housing lending, partially offset by a reduction in high-quality liquid assets (HQLA)" (ev-28, ev-26). This is a statutory-basis sub-split of NII, not an additional driver.

drivers.bank_label: Increase / (decrease) due to change in average rate
drivers.narrative: Rate effects cost $558m (ev-34), though headline NIM still rose 3bps to 1.74% from 1.71% (ev-27, ev-51): +9bps from "higher earnings on deposit and capital replicating portfolios", +2bps lower-yielding HQLA mix, +2bps Markets and Treasury, offset by -7bps "higher deposit costs including competitive pressures" and deposit mix, -2bps wholesale funding, -1bp lending margin (ev-29, ev-31, ev-32, ev-30, ev-33). Ex M&T and liquids, NIM declined 1bp (ev-51).

drivers.columns: Year to Sep 25 vs Year to Sep 24
drivers.narrative: Down "$67 million or 1.9%" to $3,415m (ev-16, ev-3). Inside it: +$74m economic hedges offset in NII, +$67m higher customer-related remediation (charge $102m vs $35m) and a $66m fee reduction "from the winding down and disposal of Group businesses"; excluding these the underlying decrease was only $8m or 0.3% (ev-16, ev-38). Net fees and commissions -$132m; trading income +$33m (underlying -$41m on "lower NAB risk management income in Markets"); other +$32m from MLC Life and FirstCape NZ (ev-35, ev-36, ev-37, ev-40, ev-41, ev-17).

drivers.bank_label: Operating expenses (excluding payroll review and remediation)
drivers.columns: Year to Sep 25 vs Year to Sep 24
drivers.narrative: UNDERLYING expenses: excluding the $130m payroll review and remediation increase, opex rose "$305 million or 3.2%" (ev-18, ev-46). Driven by "salary expense inflation, continued investment in technology and financial crime related capabilities, and investment in additional bankers", partly offset by productivity of $420m and lower AUSTRAC EU costs of $71m (ev-19, ev-47, ev-22, ev-24). The Sep24-Sep25 walk: salary +$267m, volume +$143m, technology & investment +$213m, D&A +$42m, productivity -$420m, other +$131m (incl. financial crime +$62m), EU -$71m (ev-22, ev-23). Personnel +$271m, technology +$71m, general +$81m, occupancy +$12m (ev-57, ev-58, ev-59, ev-60). Cash CTI worsened 80bps to 47.3% (ev-75); FTE +7.0% (ev-76).

drivers.columns: Year to Sep 25 vs Year to Sep 24
drivers.narrative: The FY25 headline opex increase of $435m (4.6%) includes "an increase of $130 million for payroll review and remediation costs" (ev-18, ev-25), which the CEO calls "disappointing and must be fixed" (ev-47). These are "costs associated with the ongoing program of work to identify, rectify and remediate payroll issues", $130m in FY25 (1H25 $43m, 2H25 $87m), including $33m of payments and benefits to colleagues (ev-78, ev-79). Personnel carried $101m and general expenses $29m (ev-57, ev-59). Payroll review is an FY25 increase, so the delta equals the charge.

drivers.columns: Year to Sep 25 vs Year to Sep 24
drivers.narrative: The charge "increased by $105 million or 14.4% to $833 million" from $728m, "driven by a higher level of individually assessed credit impairment charge primarily in Corporate and Institutional Banking" (ev-20, ev-63, ev-48). Individually assessed rose $328m or 51.6% to $964m, on "impairment of a small number of customers" in C&IB plus non-recurrence of FY24 write-backs and recoveries (ev-64, ev-61, ev-65). Partly offset by collective provisions swinging $223m from a $92m charge to a $131m write-back, including a $283m forward-looking release (ev-66, ev-62, ev-50). CIC/GLAs 0.11% vs 0.10% (ev-67).

drivers.bank_label: Income tax expense and non-controlling interests
drivers.columns: Year to Sep 25 vs Year to Sep 24
drivers.narrative: Income tax expense "increased by $27 million or 0.9% due to higher cash earnings before income tax and a higher effective tax rate" (ev-21, ev-42); the effective tax rate rose 10bps to 29.6% "primarily due to a decrease in the amount recognised as a deferred tax asset for U.S. tax losses", partly offset by prior-year over-provisions (ev-44, ev-43). Non-controlling interests rose from $18m to $39m, a further $21m drag (ev-9); the bank gives no reason for this. Combined -$48m.

notable_items: Payroll review and remediation costs of $130m in FY25 inside operating expenses (ev-78, ev-18)
Customer-related remediation charge in net fees and commissions of $102m in FY25 vs $35m in FY24 (ev-38)
Fee reduction of $66m from the winding down and disposal of Group businesses (ev-38, ev-16)
AUSTRAC Enforceable Undertaking costs of $18m in FY25 vs $89m in FY24, a $71m reduction (ev-24, ev-22)

Non-cash (statutory-only) items: acquisitions, integration, disposals and business closures -$295m after tax vs -$4m; hedging and fair value volatility +$28m vs -$6m (ev-11, ev-72, ev-73) — excluded from the cash bridge by design

disagreements.topic: Cash vs statutory movement FY25 v FY24
disagreements.explanation: Cash earnings excludes non-cash items. The $190m wider statutory fall is driven by acquisitions, integration, disposals and business closures (-$295m after tax vs -$4m, a $291m deterioration), a $74m smaller discontinued-operations loss and a +$34m hedging/fair value swing (ev-72, ev-73, ev-71). NAB's primary measure is cash earnings.

disagreements.topic: Total NII movement: performance table vs volume/rate analysis
disagreements.explanation: The Group performance results table prints a cash-basis NII increase of $644m (ev-14, ev-2); the average balance sheet volume and rate analysis, prepared on the statutory average balance sheet, totals $646m (ev-34). The $2m gap is a basis/scope difference, so the volume (+$1,204m) and rate (-$558m) split is used as a sub-decomposition only.

disagreements.topic: New Zealand Banking cash earnings FY25
disagreements.explanation: The results book divisional table reports New Zealand Banking in AUD ($1,353m, +1.5%) while presentation page 48 reports it in NZD local currency ($1,485m, +2.8%). Not used as a Group bridge driver either way.

limitations: NAB publishes no cash earnings waterfall for FY25 v FY24. The bridge here is assembled from the Group performance results table's stated year-on-year movements (ev-13 to ev-21), each of which the bank states against the September 2024 comparative; the components sum exactly to the -$11m movement (+644 -67 -435 -105 -27 -21), so no residual arises.

The operating expense contribution is split into UNDERLYING (-$305m, ex payroll review) and the payroll review/remediation notable (-$130m); these sum to the headline -$435m increase. The only primary walk chart (presentation p25) is an EXPENSE walk covering Sep 24 to Sep 25, not a cash earnings walk; its bars are reported inside the expense narrative rather than as separate cash earnings drivers.

The NII volume (+$1,204m) and rate (-$558m) split comes from the statutory average balance sheet volume/rate analysis and totals $646m, not the $644m cash figure; it is a sub-decomposition of the nii driver and must not be added to it.

The $74m economic hedge movement is a gross transfer between NII and other operating income and is revenue-neutral at Group level: NII's $644m increase includes a $74m decrease from hedges while other operating income's $67m fall includes a $74m increase (ev-14, ev-16). Underlying figures are $718m and -$8m respectively.
The bank gives no explanation for the $21m increase in non-controlling interests (from $18m to $39m), which is folded into tax_and_other on arithmetic alone.

Comparatives were restated during FY25 for the presentation of directly attributable income-earning expenses and for portfolio transfers between Personal Banking and Business & Private Banking (ev-5 footnotes), so FY24 figures here are restated ones.
Capped at 80: tax_and_other -48 $m. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.

evidence_records.quote: Net interest income increased by $644 million or 3.8%. This includes a decrease of $74 million due to movements in economic hedges, offset in other operating income. Excluding this movement, the underlying increase of $718 million or 4.3% was due to higher average interest earning assets and net interest margin.

The higher net interest margin was primarily due to higher earnings on deposit and capital replicating portfolios, higher Markets and Treasury income and lower mix of liquid assets. These increases were partially offset by deposit impacts, higher wholesale funding costs and lower lending margins.

Other operating income decreased by $67 million or 1.9%. This includes an increase of $74 million due to movements in economic hedges, offset in net interest income, and an increase in customer-related remediation of $67 million, together with the fee reduction impact from the winding down and disposal of Group businesses of $66 million. Excluding these movements, the underlying decrease was $8 million or 0.3%.
